candidates.explanation: The new-email verification mail most likely builds its link the same way as MailService.userSignUp. That means it uses the `/confirm-email` frontend path, and probably the `activation.hbs` template. The frontend page at that path calls `POST /auth/email/confirm`, which runs AuthService.confirmEmail. That method requires an inactive user and never applies `newEmail`. The link should point to a `/confirm-new-email` route, which calls `POST /auth/email/confirm/new` and runs AuthService.confirmNewEmail. The body of this method is elided in the snippet, so this diagnosis rests on the bug report and the sign-up code, not on the actual URL line.

This method signs the hash with `confirmEmailUserId` and `newEmail` and then calls mailService.confirmNewEmail. The call is elided in the snippet. If it sends the mail through the wrong method or with the wrong data, the user would get the sign-up style link. This is less likely than the first candidate.

fix.description: In MailService.confirmNewEmail, build the URL with `/confirm-new-email` instead of `/confirm-email`. Use the `confirm-new-email.hbs` template. The frontend route should then POST the hash to `/auth/email/confirm/new`.
